statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks were judged. Category/detail routes encountered a reproducible Cloudflare verification screen and are reported as resilience/core-flow findings rather than omitted work.

paths.description: Homepage: primary search, seasonal listing rail, categories, consent, preferences, responsive behavior, performance, security and metadata.
Transport category listing archetype; selected to represent browse/filter routes. Navigation reached a Cloudflare verification screen.
Representative item-detail archetype selected from the homepage; navigation reached a Cloudflare verification screen.
Primary seller journey entry. It resolved to the login surface and was inspected with the account path.
Account/login form archetype: labels, validation, autocomplete, recovery, and authentication options.
Failure/recovery behavior represented by the anti-bot challenge and an attempted unknown route.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent wall obscures all content on first load.
findings.evidence: At 390×844 the consent layer covers most of the viewport and blocks the search/listing content until a choice is made; desktop is also dimmed behind a large fixed panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a compact, content-preserving consent surface while keeping reject and settings equally accessible.

findings.summary: Core listing and detail journeys can be interrupted by an anti-bot challenge.
findings.evidence: Fresh navigations to both a category listing and an item detail produced a Cloudflare “verify you are not a robot” screen instead of the requested content.
findings.suggestedFix: Tune bot controls so ordinary browsing can continue, preserve session proof across routes, and provide a reliable accessible fallback.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance misses the LCP target.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.4 s, FCP 3.3 s, and performance 0.67; the trace corroborated a slower 2.84 s LCP under a separate run.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, prioritize its request, reduce consent/third-party startup work, and validate against the ≤2.5 s LCP target.

findings.summary: The viewport disables user zoom and some touch targets are too small.
findings.evidence: Viewport content includes maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed both meta-viewport and target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale/user-scalable restrictions and enlarge densely packed controls while preserving responsive reflow.

findings.summary: CSP is missing and analytics/consent cookies are not consistently Secure.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but headers found no CSP; cookie audit found 6 flagged cookies including _ga values without Secure and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a report-only then enforcing CSP and set Secure plus appropriate SameSite on all cookies.

findings.summary: The first load has a large tracking and partner footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker audit found 11 third-party origins and Hotjar, DoubleClick, GTM, and Google Analytics; the consent copy names 274 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, prevent non-essential trackers before opt-in, batch essential analytics, and document each retained processor.

findings.summary: Primary listing/detail content is not reliably available to a non-JS crawler or challenged browser.
findings.evidence: Homepage raw HTML retained 80% of rendered content, but the detail discoverability request returned HTTP 403 and the browser view was a challenge page.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful listing/detail HTML before JavaScript and allow legitimate crawlers/users through bot controls with a fallback.

findings.summary: Third-party delivery is disproportionate to the lightweight marketplace landing page.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed 1.224 MB of 1.262 MB transferred to origins other than m.skelbiu.lt, with 49 of 51 requests in that bucket.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, self-host stable first-party assets, and remove low-value trackers and font variants.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a bright white/yellow interface, and the DOM probe found no color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: The modal consent flow is built as a generic div rather than a native dialog.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found <div role="dialog" aria-modal="true"> and no native <dialog>, popover, or details primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with platform dismissal/focus behavior, or a non-modal semantic region if blocking is not required.

findings.summary: Several controls are undersized for touch, although keyboard outlines remain visible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size; the probe measured multiple navigation links only 17–19 px high while focus tests retained a browser outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive target boxes and spacing to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Render-critical delivery has a long dependency chain.
findings.evidence: HAR found five parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets plus a non-deferred consent stub; three Google fonts took 1.2–1.35 s. Lighthouse failed the network-dependency-tree insight.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline/merge critical CSS, self-host or reduce font variants, defer non-critical consent code, and preconnect only where justified.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript dominates transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: The 1.26 MB HAR attributes 534 KB to scripts; GTM alone is 184 KB and 49 of 51 requests are classified off the m.skelbiu.lt origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant trackers, load analytics after consent/idle, and code-split marketplace features by route.

findings.summary: Some content and search controls lack accessible text relationships.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt; the probe found one image without alt and the keyword input had only placeholder text rather than an associated label.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration and a persistent <label> for search.

findings.summary: Text/background contrast fails automated WCAG checks.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit scored 0 on the rendered home page.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust failing foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA and test normal, dark, and high-contrast modes.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a top-level heading and key landmarks.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero H1 elements and no main/nav/header landmarks, although sampled controls retained visible browser focus outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive H1 and semantic header, nav, and main landmarks without disturbing the visible design.

findings.summary: The page is not eligible for back/forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the BFCache audit with three failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the BFCache diagnostics and remove unload handlers or other blockers so route returns are instant and stateful.

findings.summary: Authentication remains password-centric with no passkey option.
findings.evidence: The login probe found phone/password and social providers, no WebAuthn/credential API signal, and missing autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration/authentication and retain password recovery as fallback; request any browser permissions only after a user action.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent or weak.
findings.evidence: Headers had no Permissions-Policy or CSP/frame-ancestors; Referrer-Policy is the legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade, though X-Frame-Options and HSTS are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrictive Permissions-Policy, modern strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and CSP frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: Runtime access to key routes is fragile under anti-bot rate controls.
findings.evidence: Category and detail navigations were replaced by a verification spinner after a short audit browsing sequence.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve verified state and ensure menus, listings, and details degrade to navigable server-rendered content during challenge handling.

findings.summary: Language is declared correctly, but the CSS shows no logical-property adoption.
findings.evidence: The root lang is lt and language alternatives are visible; the CSS probe found no margin-inline/padding-inline/inset-inline signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inline/block properties and set dir explicitly where translated RTL content is supported.

findings.summary: The login form does not expose actionable validation semantics on empty submission.
findings.evidence: The form fields are not required and an empty-submit probe found no :invalid elements, aria-invalid state, or role=alert message.
findings.suggestedFix: Add post-interaction validation, clear field-level messages, aria-invalid, and an announced error summary.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The login probe found blank autocomplete on phone and password inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username (or tel where appropriate) and current-password; use new-password for registration.

findings.summary: Most listing images use legacy formats without responsive sources.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 46 legacy-format images and 47 of 48 images without srcset; only 2 used modern formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and width-based srcset/sizes while retaining a compatible fallback.

findings.summary: Consent and analytics work consumes substantial bandwidth before the core task.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 368 KB from cookielaw, 184 KB from GTM, and initiated multiple analytics endpoints during the initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential vendors until consent and idle time, remove duplicate measurement, and batch analytics.

findings.summary: The consent animation ignores reduced-motion preference.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, a 400 ms onetrust-fade-in animation remained active and no reduced-motion CSS rule was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential transitions and animations in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no view-transition rules; navigation swaps are immediate and representative linked pages fall into a separate challenge screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route/state changes, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The horizontal listings carousel does not use native snapping or overscroll semantics.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found the .js-slider overflow area at 7,604 px wide with scroll-snap-type:none and overflow-x:hidden.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native horizontal scroller with scroll-snap and appropriate overscroll behavior, preserving button and keyboard controls.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The mobile page has a persistent header but the CSS probe found no scroll-state/container-query support or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries for a compact scrolled header or another position-aware cue where it improves orientation.

findings.summary: Reusable listing/category components rely on viewport layouts rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no @container rule or container-type despite cards being reused in differently sized desktop and mobile regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reused cards and category modules while retaining a conventional fallback.

findings.summary: A small number of images omit dimensions or alt text.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 2 images without dimensions and 1 without alt; doctype and UTF-8 charset were valid.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every rendered image intrinsic width/height and appropriate alt semantics.

findings.summary: The homepage has JSON-LD but no Open Graph share metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found one JSON-LD block and zero og:* tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph and Twitter card metadata matching visible marketplace content.

findings.summary: High-value marketplace actions are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: The site has search and post-listing forms but no WebMCP/agentic-form signal; robots also explicitly blocks many AI crawler user agents.
findings.suggestedFix: If agentic commerce is desired, expose tightly scoped search, save, and draft-listing tools with confirmation for consequential actions.
